metadata.rationale: Runtime version and capability queries are host adaptation rather than mathematical algorithms.
metadata.fallback: The dynamic runtime reports an unavailable capability or JavaScript implementation when the addon is absent.

exact-arithmetic.rationale: Scalar exact arithmetic and classical number-theory entry points currently adapt established FLINT, GMP, or smalljac operations.
exact-arithmetic.fallback: Ordinary Sage.js exact arithmetic remains the semantic implementation when the native package is unavailable.

algebraic.rationale: Algebraic and cyclotomic values use FLINT qqbar and number-field storage behind native conversion boundaries.
algebraic.fallback: Strict Python algebraic-number operations retain capability diagnostics and portable semantic paths.

dirichlet.rationale: Dirichlet exports mix FLINT group primitives with Sage.js-owned character orchestration and require staged separation.
dirichlet.fallback: The strict Python Dirichlet implementation is the semantic fallback for every public operation.

modular-symbols.rationale: P1 and modular-symbol exports combine packed representation primitives, retained C oracles, and Sage.js-owned algorithms.
modular-symbols.fallback: Strict Python modular-symbol code and source-transparent P1 kernels provide the semantic fallback.

dense-matrix-storage.rationale: Dense matrix constructors and packed import or export operations adapt host objects to established native storage.
dense-matrix-storage.fallback: The ordinary Matrix implementation reconstructs the same values without requiring a native object.

dense-matrix-algorithms.rationale: Dense matrix operations must separate mature FLINT algorithms from locally implemented control flow and Node conversion.
dense-matrix-algorithms.fallback: The portable matrix backend and ordinary Matrix methods remain correctness fallbacks.

extension-fields.rationale: Finite extension-field values, polynomials, and matrices are adapters to mature FLINT fq algorithms and resources.
extension-fields.fallback: Ordinary finite-field code retains correct behavior or an explicit native capability diagnostic.

multivariate.rationale: Multivariate polynomial operations adapt mature FLINT and Groebner implementations through native resources.
multivariate.fallback: Strict Python polynomial objects preserve public semantics when the native capability is absent.

polynomials.rationale: Univariate polynomial exports primarily adapt mature FLINT algorithms and packed coefficient representations.
polynomials.fallback: Ordinary polynomial arithmetic remains the tested semantic fallback.

numerical.rationale: Real, complex, and special-function exports adapt MPFR, MPC, Arb, and FLINT numerical algorithms.
numerical.fallback: The portable numerical layer preserves explicit precision semantics or reports a capability boundary.

elliptic.rationale: Elliptic-curve exports combine smalljac, a pinned eclib 2-descent source closure, Arb/Acb L-function primitives, and Sage.js-owned point and coefficient conversion.
elliptic.fallback: Strict Python elliptic-curve arithmetic and split-Mellin L-series evaluation remain semantic fallbacks; database ranks remain available and unsupported native-only rank computation reports its capability boundary.

graph.rationale: Graph exports adapt mature igraph algorithms and opaque graph storage through the graph native package.
graph.fallback: The ordinary graph implementation remains available without the igraph capability.

matrix_remediation.policy: Every registered export is assigned exactly once below. Representation boundaries are retained, thin or mature-library operations move behind declarations, and Sage.js-owned control flow is an explicit typed-Python migration exception.

representation-primitives.rationale: These exports construct, import, export, or convert opaque dense storage. They remain replaceable host adapters while packed host-neutral ABIs are expanded.

foreign-and-thin-bridges.rationale: These callbacks are primarily mature FLINT operations or small storage transformations. Their stable mathematical ABI belongs in declarations, not handwritten Node-specific registration.

source-owned-algorithm-exceptions.rationale: These callbacks contain Sage.js-owned traversal, ordering, normalization, multimodular, sparse, or mixed-ring control flow. Existing C stays frozen as an explicit differential oracle until the required typed storage is production-ready.

exports.note: The source-transparent production path retains this callback solely as a differential and performance oracle.
